description:
**Monday Immune Engager** — our weekly pick from the latest immune-engager digest.

**[T cell–mediated antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity provides a therapeutic approach for solid cancers](https://doi.org/10.1172/jci.insight.205984)**

*JCI Insight, 2026*

DOI: [10.1172/jci.insight.205984](https://doi.org/10.1172/jci.insight.205984)

**Question:** Can the native FcγRI signalling module's antigen-density threshold make redirected T cell killing tumour-selective?

**Answer:** AG2G T cells signalled only above ~50 HER2 molecules/µm² on bilayers and spared primary human epithelium that matched HER2 CAR T cells killed; in vitro and NSG xenografts only, no immunocompetent safety data.

**Three takeaways**

1. FcγRI clustering needs ~50 molecules/µm²; TCR signals at 10–20 and the matched HER2 CAR down to 10 — a 2.5- to 5-fold higher bar.
2. On one HT29 line, cetuximab (high EGFR) killed, trastuzumab (borderline HER2) killed weakly, anti-MUC16 (low) not at all; matched HER2 CAR T cells killed primary human epithelium where AG2G did not.
3. Selectivity is shown in dishes and immunodeficient mice, and the stated threshold is 30/µm² in the abstract but ~50 in the results.

source_metadata.digest_excerpt:
## Top Papers

### 1. T cell-mediated antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity provides a therapeutic approach for solid cancers

Richter A, Dotan S, Shendrik P, Rasoulouniriana D, Zarfin A, Santana-Magal N, et al.

*JCI Insight*

[10.1172/jci.insight.205984](https://doi.org/10.1172/jci.insight.205984)

Any IgG-opsonised tumour antigen × CD8 T cell; a modified FcγRI receptor expressed in T cells rather than a soluble bispecific.

The chronic problem for engager design is not potency but the absence of binary tumour-restricted antigens, and this paper attacks the problem from the signalling side instead of the binder side. Starting from an observation that CD8 T cells at inflammatory sites trogocytose FcγRI from monocytes and transiently kill by antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity, the authors measured the activation threshold and found that FcγRI phosphorylation only occurs above roughly thirty antigen molecules per square micrometre — a genuine density switch rather than a graded response. Engineering that receptor into peripheral blood CD8 T cells produced cells that killed tumour cells while sparing healthy tissue carrying the same antigen at physiological density, and the receptor also reduced basement-membrane adhesion and improved tumour infiltration. For anyone building engagers, the transferable claim is that antigen density, not antigen identity, can be made the selectivity filter, and that the threshold is a property of the signalling module that can be tuned.

DICE score: 4 — Converts antigen density into an engineered, measurable activation threshold for redirected killing, which is a different route to the therapeutic window than affinity or format tuning.

Tel Aviv University with Dustin (Kennedy Institute) and Spitzer (UCSF/Gladstone).
source_metadata.abstract:
The clinical success of chimeric antigen receptor T cells in treating hematological malignancies has highlighted the immense therapeutic potential of engineering T cells with synthetic receptors. However, the limited availability of tumor-specific antigens and the poor ability of T cells to infiltrate solid tumor cores remain major obstacles for applying this approach to solid tumors. In this study, we identify a subset of CD8
                    +
                    T cells at inflammatory sites that acquire FcγRI through trogocytosis from infiltrating monocytes, enabling them to perform transient TCR-independent antibody-dependent cellular cytotoxicity (ADCC). Analysis of FcγRI signaling in these T cells revealed that phosphorylation occurs only when antigen density on the membrane exceeds 30 molecules/μm². Exploiting this threshold, we engineered peripheral blood CD8
                    +
                    T cells to express a modified FcγRI receptor, allowing them to selectively kill tumor cells while largely sparing healthy tissues expressing normal physiological levels of the same antigen. Moreover, expression of FcγRI receptor in T cells was associated with reduced basement membrane interactions, enhancing their capacity to infiltrate tumors and establish long-term immune memory. Collectively, this work establishes T cell–mediated ADCC as a potent therapeutic strategy that leverages antigen density, rather than antigen identity, to achieve selective cancer targeting.
